messages:
Alex W.: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector tweak we're seeing a regression on multi-GPU runs (8xA100). Token tail latency up ~15% under the long-seq workload. I ran an nsys capture and the NCCL all-reduces look serialized instead of overlapping. Anyone else hit this?

Priya R.: Yup, same on canary. Repro is stable. Timeline shows back-to-back all-reduces anchored to rank0 timings, looks like a global serialization point.

Samir: Noted. The selector now prefers the fused-attn kernel for seq=1024 when quantized (commit 8a3f7). That kernel runs longer per-token but shouldn't force NCCL ordering unless we introduced an explicit sync/flush.

Emily H.: Uploaded my captures: I ran `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nccl,nvtx --output=selector_regress_ns ./run_inference.sh` and also a perfetto dump. On the nvtx timeline I see repeated `batch_flush` markers immediately before each NCCL all-reduce — as if the runtime flushes pending batches prior to collectives. Also KV cache eviction spikes line up with the longer kernels.

Jorge M.: Hypothesis: the longer fused kernel increases KV cache refill cadence and the batching heuristic now forces flushes more aggressively. That batch_flush may be inserting a stream sync that serializes NCCL. But why would flush be NVTX-wrapped as a sync?

Alex W.: Snippet from the timeline I pasted to the GCS bucket (gs://redwood-profiles/1864001234-selector-regress/):
```
[2026-03-15 14:12:03] NVTX: batch_build start
[2026-03-15 14:12:03] NVTX: kernel:fused_attn_qkv
[2026-03-15 14:12:03] NVTX: batch_flush
[2026-03-15 14:12:03] NCCL: allReduce start
```
That batch_flush NVTX always precedes the allReduce on all ranks.

Priya R.: Repro steps I'm using: 8-gpu, batch_size=1 per rank, seq_len=1024. If I set env RUNTIME_BATCH_FLUSH_THRESHOLD=0.8 (old default) concurrency comes back and tail latency goes down. The new default is 0.4 — looks like the heuristic was tightened in the same PR chain.

Samir: So two suspects: the kernel selection (longer kernel time) and the batching heuristic change. Either could cause earlier flushes. We should also look at NCCL algorithm/topology — sometimes different launch patterns + occupancy changes make NCCL pick a non-overlapping algo. Run with `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` to see chosen algo.

Emily H.: I'll capture NCCL debug and topology: `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO NCCL_P2P_LEVEL=NVL run_inference.sh` and re-run nsys. Also will attach KV cache counters (hits/misses) to the nvtx timeline so we can correlate.

Jorge M.: Good. Another angle: NVTX annotations themselves shouldn't block, but if batch_flush performs `cudaDeviceSynchronize()` or uses stream wait events incorrectly that could. Check runtime flush implementation: I think the flush does `cudaEventRecord` + `cudaStreamWaitEvent` on the collective stream — maybe it uses a blocking host sync in the path.

Alex W.: Plan: bisect the selector commit and toggle the heuristic flag independently. Steps: 1) revert kernel-selector commit -> profile; 2) keep selector but revert flush-threshold -> profile; 3) reapply both and try async-flush change. I'll need 8xA100 for 2h to run controlled experiments.

infra-bot: Reservation request accepted — cluster-gpu-8 reserved 2h starting 2026-03-16 09:00 UTC :white_check_mark:

Emily H.: Small repro I used (so others can run quickly):
```bash
export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
export RUNTIME_BATCH_FLUSH_THRESHOLD=0.4 # test value
nsys profile --trace=cuda,nccl,nvtx --output=tmp ./bench_infer --gpus 8 --seq 1024 --batch 1
```
If you flip the threshold to 0.8 the all-reduce overlap returns in my runs.

Priya R.: Quick suggestion: add an nvtx marker just before and after `cudaStreamWaitEvent` in flush path — if we see host-blocking, it will show up. Also consider temporarily removing the NVTX marker `batch_flush` to check if the marker itself hides behavior in perf viewers.

Samir: If ordering is the root cause we can change kernel launcher to use non-blocking enqueue semantics: launch fused kernel on its stream, don't call `cudaStreamSynchronize` on the compute stream, and use events to order only when necessary. That should let NCCL overlap.

Jorge M.: Also try forcing NCCL algorithm: `NCCL_ALGO=ring` or `NCCL_COLLNET_DISABLE=1` to see if a different algorithm improves overlap — that helps narrow whether it's an NCCL decision or runtime-imposed sync.

Alex W.: I'll start the bisect tomorrow and post links to each nsys + perfetto capture. If we confirm it's the heuristic, we can either revert or add an adaptive threshold keyed by kernel latency. If it's kernel selection that causes problematic ordering we may need a fast-path kernel or split the fused kernel.

Emily H.: I'm going to prototype an async-flush branch that records an event and queues the all-reduce without host blocking. Will post PR when I have a bench.

Priya R.: Note for release notes: if we revert the heuristic we should call it out as a regression fix for multi-GPU tail latency.

Alex W.: Thanks all — good triage. Keep uploads in the GCS folder and tag captures with `bisect-step-*`. Ping me if you need the reservation bumped. :thumbsup:

Jorge M.: I'll also generate perfetto flame graphs across all ranks and put a combined HTML in the bucket. :eyes:

Samir: If anyone needs a quick flame graph script, use `nsys export --format=tracing` then `perfetto --import` — I can paste my helper script.

Alex W.: OK wrapping up here. Following up with results after the bisect. Thanks! :rocket:
